pairs.reason: Implementation 2's exact-Fraction arithmetic with the str() round-trip trick and its NaN/inf rejection are clever and a bit more robust, but they add machinery and behavior the task never asked for. Implementation 1 meets the spec simply, with correct boundary handling and good tests.

The two behave the same: both check the source unit's literal absolute zero and both short-circuit when the units match. Implementation 1 is more compact, while Implementation 2 groups each unit's data together and has more targeted tests (same-unit exactness, the source-unit boundary, the unit named in the error), though its data is defined below the function that uses it.

Implementation 1 has no same-unit shortcut, so converting K to K (or F to F) can come back with float noise, while Implementation 2 returns the value unchanged and tests that. Implementation 1 does handle unhashable unit inputs more gracefully, but that edge case matters less.
